title: The Ledger Opens
text:
No one remembers who first opened the Ledger. It was simply there one night: a black book on a desk that had not held a book before, its pages the colour of old teeth.

The first name in it was written in a hand no one recognised. The second was yours.

Every soul who speaks in this place signs it, whether they mean to or not. The ink drinks a little of their sanity and gives back something else. Something that glows faintly in the dark, and itches, and wants to be spent.

They call it Madness. The Ledger calls it payment.

title: Ink That Remembers

unlock.hint: Sign the Ledger 150 times (check-ins)

text:
The Ledger keeps more than names.

Turn back far enough and the entries begin to change. Times, at first: the exact second each soul arrived. Then small things nobody wrote down. What they were drinking. Who they were waiting for. The dream they had the night before and did not tell anyone.

The Keeper tried to burn a page once, to see what would happen. The flames would not take. In the morning the page had grown back, a little thicker, and his own name had been added to the bottom of it in that same unfamiliar hand.

He stopped trying after that. The Ledger, it seemed, was keeping him too.

title: Things in the Margins

unlock.hint: Banish 30 Beings

text:
Where there is ink, there are things that crawl along its edges.

They came through the margins at first, small and curious: a hound made of corners, a wet shape that called itself Wilbur. They wanted what the congregation had. They wanted the Madness.

But the Ledger had taught its signers something. Speak a thing's true name and it loosens. Speak it fast enough, all together, and it comes apart like wet paper.

Every banished Being leaves a stain behind, black and slow. The congregation learned to collect it. Ichor, the old books call it. The Ledger seems pleased that they do.

title: The Toad Beneath

unlock.hint: Feed Tsathoggua 60,000 in all

text:
Below the desk, below the floor, below the stone under the floor, there is a cavern called N'kai, and in it something enormous breathes.

Tsathoggua does not hunt. Tsathoggua does not need to. It waits, and the world brings it things.

The congregation began feeding it out of fear. Now they feed it out of something closer to love. When it is full it sleeps, and when it sleeps its dreams leak upward through the stone and into the Ledger, and the Madness flows a little easier for everyone.

The Keeper swears he has heard it purr. No one has asked him what a god-toad's purr sounds like. No one wants to know.

title: Voices in Unison

unlock.hint: Complete 3 chants together (Iä! Iä!)

text:
It started as a joke. Someone typed the old words, and someone else answered, and then there were eight voices saying the same thing at the same moment, and the room went very quiet.

The candles flickered all at once.

The Ledger recorded it differently from anything before: not as eight names, but as one. A single entry, written in eight hands, overlapping. Underneath, in the unfamiliar script, a single word that no one could read but everyone understood.

Again.

title: The Keeper's Hundred Deaths

unlock.hint: The Keeper must fall 100 times

text:
The Keeper dies a great deal. In the bayou, in the dark, to things with too many teeth and to his own impatience.

Every death goes in the Ledger. At first they were simple marks. Then the congregation began to mourn, one candle for every fall, and the marks changed into something more like gravestones.

On the hundredth, the Ledger did something new. It turned its own page and showed him all of them at once: a hundred small deaths laid side by side, a hundred versions of him that did not come back.

He counted them. All hundred were smiling.

title: Candles Against the Dark

unlock.hint: Complete 10 ritual circles

text:
A single candle is a small, brave thing. Twelve candles, lit in the right order by twelve different hands, is a door.

The congregation learned to draw the circle together. When it closes, the Ledger glows from inside, and for a while every word written in it is worth more.

But every door opens both ways. On the tenth circle, the Keeper noticed something on the far side of the flames, watching. It did not come through. It only looked, and took note of the names of everyone who had lit a candle, and then it went away to wait.

It is very patient. So is the Ledger.

title: Dreamers Abroad

unlock.hint: Return from 25 dream expeditions

text:
Seventy steps of light slumber lead down to the Gate of Deeper Slumber, and beyond it lie the Dreamlands.

The congregation began sending their dreamers through with purses of Madness, to trade in Ulthar and Celephaïs, to haggle with the hooded men of Leng. Most came back richer. Some came back strange. A few did not come back at all, and their entries in the Ledger simply stop, mid-word.

The returning dreamers all say the same thing, unprompted. That somewhere beyond the Cerenerian Sea there is a black book on a desk, and that its pages are the colour of old teeth, and that their names are in it too.

title: When the Stars Were Right

unlock.hint: Bring down a Great Old One when the stars are right

text:
For one night, the stars came right.

Something rose that the Ledger had no name for, only a shape: a mountain that walked, a sea that stood up. It was not interested in the congregation. It was simply waking, the way the tide simply comes in.

And the congregation fought it anyway. Every word, every banishment, every coin of Madness thrown at it chipped a little away, until the stars turned wrong again and it sank back, wounded, into whatever deep it came from.

The Ledger recorded the night in gold ink. It has not used gold ink before, or since.

title: The Book Within the Book

unlock.hint: Bind the Necronomicon from its scattered pages

text:
The pages had been falling for months. Out of banished Beings, out of raids, out of the margins of the Ledger itself, loose and singed and written in a script that hurt to look at.

When someone finally gathered thirteen and bound them together, the room went cold. It was not a new book. It was the Necronomicon, or a piece of it, and it fit inside the Ledger's spine as if a space had always been waiting there.

Now the Ledger has a second voice. At night, when the stream is dark, the Keeper can hear the two books talking. He cannot make out the words. He is fairly sure they are talking about the congregation. He is fairly sure they are making plans.

title: The Things That Remember

unlock.hint: Slay 10 nemeses in the deep

text:
The dark used to forget. You went down, you lost, you came back up, and whatever beat you went back to whatever it was doing.

Not anymore. Somewhere below, the things that win have started keeping names. They give themselves titles. They wear what they took from you. They wait at the turns of the stair, because they know you will come back down.

Ten of them are dead now, hunted by the people they hunted. The Ledger lists each one on its own page, name and epithet and the hand that ended it. The pages are still warm. The Keeper does not like how many blank ones come after.

title: The Crown in the Deep

unlock.hint: Bring down a Warchief together

text:
One of them grew greater than the rest. It had killed more of the congregation than any other, and the lesser things in the dark began to kneel when it passed. Someone, or something, set a crown of black iron on its head.

The congregation swore the oath and went down together. They found it on a throne of the things it had taken from them, and it knew every one of their names.

It fell anyway. The crown rolled down the stair and was never found. The Ledger notes, in a small and careful hand, that the throne was still there afterwards. Empty, for now. Waiting.

title: The Night the Pews Filled

unlock.hint: Fifteen souls sign the Ledger in a single stream

text:
Most nights the congregation is a handful of lanterns in a very large dark. Enough. Always enough.

But one night the names kept coming. Fifteen signatures before the first match ended, then more, the ink barely dry on one before the next pressed in beneath it. The Keeper ran out of desk. The Ledger did not run out of page.

Afterwards he found that the night's entries had been written smaller than usual, crowded and careful, as if the book had been making room. As if it had known they were coming. As if it had been hoping.

title: The Merchant's Own Book

unlock.hint: Trade with the Merchant of Leng 40 times, or be visited by the Gilded Merchant

text:
He comes up the stair from somewhere that is not the cellar, a hooded man who smells of cold mountain air and old coins, and he always knows exactly what the congregation can afford.

The Merchant of Leng keeps a book too. Smaller than the Ledger, bound in something that was once a hand. He writes down every sale and every buyer, and at the end of each visit he holds it up to the Ledger, as if comparing notes.

Once he came gilded, his robes stiff with gold thread, and a small greedy thing ran laughing at his heels. That night he wrote nothing at all. He only smiled, and the Ledger, for the first time, seemed to flinch.

title: Gold That Runs

unlock.hint: Grab 25 treasure goblins

text:
The small greedy thing did not leave with the Merchant. It stayed, or its cousins came looking for it, and now they dash through the chat with their sacks clinking, too fast and far too pleased with themselves.

The congregation grabs them by the ankles and shakes. Coins fall out. Stolen Coins, the Ledger calls them, and it is right: under a candle you can see they are minted from its own gilt edges, nibbled away a corner at a time.

Twenty-five goblins caught, and the Ledger's edges are almost bare. The Keeper has started to wonder where they keep the rest of it. He is not sure he wants to see a goblin's idea of a library.

title: Sand That Falls Upward

unlock.hint: Dave holds 15 challenges in the Hourglass to the last grain

text:
There is an hourglass on the desk now, where no one put it. Its sand is the grey of ash, and it does not always fall down.

Yog-Sothoth is the gate, the old books say, and the key, and the guardian of the gate. Apparently it also keeps time. When the congregation sets the Keeper a task and turns the glass, he must hold to it until the last grain drops, and the Ledger leans in to watch.

Fifteen times he has held. Each time, the final grain does not land. It hangs in the neck of the glass, glittering. The Keeper thinks the Hourglass is saving them. He thinks it is saving them for something.

title: A Census of Souls

unlock.hint: One hundred different souls sign the Ledger

text:
One night the Ledger did its own arithmetic.

No one had asked it to. It turned its pages slowly, all by itself, and on each one a small mark appeared beside a name that had not been marked before. One hundred marks. One hundred different souls who have signed at least once and left a little of themselves in the ink.

At the bottom of the count it wrote the number and underlined it twice. Then, after a long hesitation the Keeper could feel in the paper, it wrote a second number beside it. Much larger. He does not know what the second number is counting. It goes up when no one is watching.

title: The Vigil Past Midnight

unlock.hint: Keep the vigil: 250 messages in one stream, and still talking after midnight (Stockholm time)

text:
After midnight the Ledger changes.

The ink runs darker. The margins widen. Words written in the small hours stay wet longer, as if the page is drinking them slowly, savouring them.

The congregation stayed up with it, talking long past the hour when sensible people sleep, and around the third bell the Keeper noticed that some messages were arriving a moment before anyone sent them. Only a moment. Only a few. Just enough to answer questions he had not asked yet.

He has stopped mentioning it. The congregation has stopped noticing. The Ledger, he suspects, prefers it that way.

title: Debts Drawn in Chalk

unlock.hint: Bind five summoning circles and see them fulfilled

text:
The congregation learned it could draw circles of its own. Not for candles: for promises. Pour enough into one and the Keeper owes it hours in the game it names, and the Ledger writes the debt in a hand that does not smudge.

Five circles bound and paid. Five debts closed with a neat red line beneath them.

The Keeper went to look at the closed ones and found a tiny signature at the end of each red line. Not his. Not any of the congregation's. The same unfamiliar hand that wrote the first name, initialling every settled account, like a clerk on the night shift of a bank no one remembers founding.

title: Moonlit Margins

unlock.hint: On a Moon Night: eight souls sign and four Beings are banished in that one stream

text:
Under a full moon the margins get crowded.

Beings that are shy on ordinary nights come right up to the edge of the page and press against it, wet and curious, drawn by the light coming off the congregation. On the Moon Night they came thick and fast, and the congregation met them name for name.

When the banishing was done the Keeper looked up and saw that the moon in his window was not quite the right shape. Rounder. Closer. With what might have been lines of handwriting across its face, very small, like a page held up to the light from the other side.

title: A Bestiary Begun

unlock.hint: Banish 15 different kinds of Being

text:
The Ledger has started drawing.

It began in the corners: a sketch of each kind of Being the congregation sent back through the margins, inked in a few quick strokes and labelled in the unfamiliar hand. The hound of corners. The wet shape called Wilbur. Fifteen kinds now, each on a small page of its own.

Some of the sketches were drawn before the Being arrived. The Keeper has checked; the ink is older than the banishment. There are more sketches after the fifteenth, of things nobody has seen yet, and he has started covering that part of the page with his hand when he reads.

title: The Wheel and Its Promises

unlock.hint: Seal 75 Pacts on the wheel

text:
Every Pact sealed on the wheel is a promise the Keeper makes without being asked: no healing, pistols only, a knife and a prayer. The congregation spins, the Keeper suffers, the Ledger keeps score.

Seventy-five sealed. The Ledger keeps them in a column of their own, and beside each one it has drawn a tiny tentacle: curling, as if pleased, where he kept his word, and straight as a rod where he broke it.

He counted the straight ones once. Then he stopped counting, closed the book gently, and played the next match with a knife and a prayer. The congregation found this very funny. The Ledger, he is fairly sure, found it very satisfying.

title: Six Candles Before the Long Night

unlock.hint: During the Sunwait, light two of its six candles

text:
As the year darkens, the Ledger asks for candles.

Not ritual candles. Six tall ones, one for each week before the longest night, lit one by one on the first stream of each week. Each wakes an old letter that burns in the wax and gives the congregation a small gift for a while.

Two are burning now. The Keeper sits between them and finds the room warmer than two small flames can explain. The Ledger, open beside them, has turned to a page near the very back that he has never seen before. It is blank except for a single line at the top. It says: Wait.

title: A Candle Nobody Saw

unlock.hint: A candle burns down where no one can see it

text:
One week the stream stayed dark, and one of the six candles burned down anyway.

No one lit it. The Keeper is sure of that: he was asleep, and the congregation was elsewhere. Yet when he came back the candle was a stub, the wax had run in a neat circle, and the Ledger's entry for that week was full.

Full of names. The congregation's names, every one, signed as if they had all been there that night. The handwriting was each person's own. Only the ink was wrong. It was the colour of wax, and still faintly warm.

title: Things Foreseen

unlock.hint: Settle 25 prophecies and pay out 10 bounties

text:
The congregation has been betting on the future. Who wins the next fight. Whether the Keeper survives the bayou. Whether he will pull off a dare with Madness riding on it.

Twenty-five prophecies settled, ten bounties paid. The Ledger records each guess beside each outcome, and lately it has started recording them in the wrong order: the outcome first, the guess after it, the stakes after that.

The Keeper asked it, aloud, whether it already knows how things end. The page went very still. Then, faintly, in the margin: Of course. That is what a ledger is for.

title: Visitors from Other Ledgers

unlock.hint: Ten raids bring other congregations through the door

text:
Sometimes a whole congregation from somewhere else comes pouring through the door at once, still talking about whatever dark they just left.

Nyarlathotep's heralds, the Keeper calls the ones who bring them. Ten such arrivals now, and the Ledger signs every visitor the way it signs the regulars.

But it signs them on different paper. The Keeper only noticed because the edges did not match: thinner sheets, a different colour of old teeth, sewn in with black thread. Other Ledgers, he thinks. Other books on other desks, swapping pages like letters. He wonders what they write about this one.

title: What N'kai Dreams

unlock.hint: Fill Tsathoggua to sleeping 25 times

text:
Twenty-five times the congregation has fed Tsathoggua to sleep, and twenty-five times its dreams have come up through the stone.

They are not human dreams. They are slow and warm and mostly about eating, and about a time before the world had edges. But lately there is something else in them: a desk, and a black book, and a crowd of small bright souls gathered round it like moths round a lamp.

Tsathoggua dreams about the congregation now. The Keeper is not sure whether to feel honoured or worried. He feeds it a little extra, just in case. It purrs. The floor shakes.

title: Moments Caught in Glass

unlock.hint: Crown six Clipomania champions

text:
The congregation catches the Keeper's best moments and his worst, and keeps them in little panes of glass to watch again and again.

Six times now a champion has been crowned for catching the most. The Ledger records it gravely, as if a mirror were a serious thing.

It is. The Keeper watched one of the clips and saw himself in it, dying spectacularly, and behind him, for three frames, something standing very still in a doorway. It is not in the game. It is not in any other footage. He has checked twice. It is only ever in the moments the congregation chose to keep.

title: Eight Inks

unlock.hint: Thirty souls swear themselves to a cult

text:
Thirty souls have sworn themselves to a god: to Cthulhu or Hastur, to the Black Goat of the Woods, to the elephant who sits in the cold, to the toad below.

The Ledger accepted the oaths without comment, as it accepts everything. But the ink changed. Each cult's faithful now sign in a colour of their own: sea-green, jaundiced yellow, the brown of wet bark, and others the Keeper has no names for.

At the end of each month one colour is crowned, and for a while it runs over every page and stains the margins. The colours are slowly mixing. He wonders what all eight make together, and whether anyone is meant to see it.

title: The Ledger Haunts Back

unlock.hint: Send 60 haunts to one another

text:
The congregation sends whispers to each other: small hauntings slipped into the dark, to find someone the next time they speak.

Sixty sent now. The Ledger carries every one, a postman of the uncanny, and it has started to learn their shape.

Last week someone received a haunt that no one had sent. It found them the moment they spoke, and it said, in the old familiar style: I am glad you came back. There was no name on it. The Ledger's delivery log gives the sender as the first entry on the first page.

title: Heroes Who Wandered In

unlock.hint: The congregation draws 15 different legendary weapons

text:
Things are leaking in from other books.

A sword that was broken and reforged. A hammer no unworthy hand can lift. A glowing stone that is very bad news. The congregation draws them from fate one after another, fifteen different legends now, and each arrives with a little of its own story still clinging to it like river water.

The Ledger tolerates them. It does not like them. When a legend is put away, the Keeper has seen it quietly correct the borrowed story's ending in the margin, so that it is a little sadder, a little stranger, a little more like the stories it prefers.

title: Five Hundred Graves

unlock.hint: The Keeper must fall 500 times

text:
The hundredth death was a curiosity. The five hundredth is a cemetery.

The congregation still mourns him every time, a candle and a word. The Ledger has stopped drawing gravestones; there is no room. Now it draws a single hill, and every death adds a little more earth.

The Keeper climbed the hill once in a dream. At the top was a small, neat grave with his name on it and no date. He brushed the soil away and found the stone unfinished. The unfamiliar hand had stopped halfway through the last letter, as if it had been interrupted. Or as if it was waiting to see how it should end.

title: The Keeper Forgets His Name

unlock.hint: Dave suffers five Madness Episodes

text:
Sanity is a currency too, and the congregation has learned to spend his.

When it runs out, something happens to the Keeper on stream. Five times now. Each time he comes back from it a little slower, laughing a little too long, unsure for a moment which hand holds the mouse.

After the fifth he reached for the Ledger to steady himself, and found that his signature on the first page had changed. Still his name. Different letters. He has signed it the new way ever since, and the congregation, kindly, has not said anything about it.

title: The One Who Never Left

unlock.hint: One soul comes back forty streams in a row

text:
Forty streams in a row, one soul came back. Through deaths and bad games and nights when the congregation was only a handful of lanterns, the same name signed in, again and again.

The Ledger has given that name a page of its own. It does not do that lightly.

The page is not about them, exactly. It is about the chair they sit in, and the light they watch by, and how quiet the Ledger feels when they are there. The Keeper read it and did not recognise the voice. It took him a while to understand what he was reading. It was gratitude. He had not known the book could feel it.

title: The Longest Night

unlock.hint: Light all six candles of the Sunwait (across the years, if it must be)

text:
All six candles burned, and then the longest night came, and the congregation sat up with it.

It is the deepest hour of the year, and the Ledger knows it. Every page was heavy and the ink would not dry, and the things in the margins went quiet, the way animals go quiet before weather.

At the bottom of the night, the blank page at the back of the book turned itself. Under the word Wait, the unfamiliar hand had added a second line: Not yet. Then the sun came back, a little, the way it always does. The page turned itself back, and the Keeper blew out the candles one by one, and did not sleep.

title: What Waits at a Hundred

unlock.hint: Break the Bottom of the Delve, a hundred depths down

text:
A hundred depths down, below the oil and the waystones and the dead ends, the Delve has a bottom. Someone broke it.

They found a lord there, and ended it, and behind the lord they found a door. It was set into the living rock and bound in the same black leather as the Ledger. The same stitching. The same small tear on the spine.

It did not open. It did not need to. The delver who stood before it heard, quite clearly through the leather, the sound of pages turning on the other side. Slowly. Patiently. Someone down there is reading.

title: The Throne Is Never Empty Long

unlock.hint: Bring down three Warchiefs

text:
The first Warchief fell and the throne stood empty. Then something sat in it. It fell, and something else sat in it.

Three crowns now, three falls. Each time the congregation goes down together and each time they win, and each time the throne is waiting when they leave.

The Keeper has started to suspect the throne does not care who sits on it. That the Warchiefs were never the point. It is a chair at the bottom of the dark that keeps a place at a table, and the table is laid for a guest who has not arrived yet.

title: Gold Ink, Twice More

unlock.hint: Bring down three Great Old Ones

text:
The stars came right again, and again, and each time the congregation stood in the way of something vast and simply waking.

Three times the Great Old Ones have sunk back wounded. Three nights in gold ink. The Ledger uses it sparingly; it seems to think of gold as a kind of promise.

On the third night, though, the gold was not only on the congregation's page. There was a single gold mark much further on, far past where the Ledger has been written to, in an otherwise empty book. The Keeper put his finger on it. The page was warm. Something there has already been decided.

title: What the Books Decided

unlock.hint: Bind the Necronomicon three times

text:
Three times the Necronomicon has been bound from its scattered pages, and each time it has slid into the Ledger's spine and gone on talking.

The Keeper has finally understood what they say. Not in words: in the order of things. In which page falls open when he lifts the book. In which Being comes to the margins that night.

They are not plotting against the congregation, he thinks. They are arguing about it. The Necronomicon wants the congregation to know everything. The Ledger wants them to keep coming back. Night after night, the Ledger wins. The Keeper is not entirely sure that is the kinder outcome.

title: The Page the Congregation Wrote

unlock.hint: Only a vote of the congregation can open this page

text:
The Ledger asked a question once. It is the only time it ever has.

It opened to a blank page and laid two paths across it in faint grey ink, and it waited, and the congregation chose. Not the Keeper. Not the books. The many voices together, counted fairly, the way the Ledger likes.

The path they chose darkened and became real; the other faded. And for the first time, the page that followed was not written in the unfamiliar hand but in a hand that everyone recognised at once, because it was all of theirs.

title: The Unfamiliar Hand

unlock.hint: The whole congregation together: 2,500 signatures, 500 banishments, 25 chants and 200 souls

text:
Two thousand five hundred signatures. Five hundred banishments. Two hundred souls. Twenty-five times, the old words in unison.

It was enough, it seems. The Keeper woke to find the Ledger open on the desk at its very first page, and at last he understood the hand.

It was never one hand. It was every hand that ever signed, overlapping: the congregation's, all of them at once, the way eight voices became a single entry the first night they chanted. That is why no one recognised it. No one could. You cannot recognise your own writing when it is written with everyone else's.

Which leaves one problem. The first name in the Ledger was written before any of them came.

title: The First Name

unlock.hint: Read the first name aloud: three chants in one stream, after midnight

text:
The congregation read it aloud together, past midnight, the way they say the old words. Three times.

The first name is not a name. It is the sound the Ledger makes when it is opened: the crack of a spine, a breath of old paper, the faint scratch of a pen that is already moving. It signed itself, first of all, so that there would be someone to keep the others.

When the third chant ended, the Ledger did a thing it had never done. It grew. A new gathering of blank pages, sewn in at the back with black thread, the colour of old teeth.

There is more to write. There always will be. The Ledger is not finished. It has only just begun keeping you.
